description: This app's own two commands, plus scoped doors: the window may ask the OS to open the project's issue tracker and the three Calibre and Kindle Previewer download pages the KFX checklist links to, and to ask the updater plugin to check, download and install. The updater grant has no allow-list to write; its scope is the one endpoint in tauri.conf.json. Four bare grants besides the doors: process:allow-restart, so the window can restart itself after an update once the engine is idle (the plugin's exit is not granted); core:window:allow-start-dragging, so the strip along the top of the page, and the gaps in the tab bar, can move it; dialog:allow-open, so the window can show a native folder picker for where books are saved; and dialog:allow-save, so it can show a save box for where a copy goes. Neither dialog grant has an allow-list to write: the user picks in the OS's own dialog, and the window only hands the path it gets back to the engine, which is what writes anything. The shell plugin is still used only from Rust; pick_file stays a Rust command. The window no longer reveals a file itself: the engine's reveal verb does that, so Show in Finder follows the library wherever it is. See ADR 2026-09-21: doors, not commands.
